authors: Dionysios Malas, Carlo Seneci, Ross Henry, Nikola Fisher, Lyndon da Cruz, Wenfeng Xia, Alberto Arezzo, Sebastien Ourselin, Christos Bergeles
abstract: The precision and flexibility of Concentric Tube Robots (CTRs) makes them well-suited for delicate surgeries and complex tasks in constrained environments, such as minimally invasive procedures. However, traditional CTRs can be bulky, as actuation typically requires multiple motors directly connected to the individual tubes. To reduce the system’s footprint, this paper proposes and evaluates remote actuation (from 1 m away) of concentric tubes using torque cables. First, we investigate the theoretical framework influencing torque transmission. Second, on a two-tube, balanced pair CTR prototype, we demonstrate the method’s performance in terms of tracing target positions and overall teleoperation ability. This study highlights the advantages and challenges of remote actuation, addressing key considerations and trade-offs when implementing this approach, and, critically, allows for miniaturising CTRs to deploy them closer to the target site without being limited by bulky actuation units.

title: Task Parameter Extrapolation via Learning Inverse Tasks From Forward Demonstrations
authors: Serdar Bahar, Fatih Dogangun, Matteo Saveriano, Yukie Nagai, Emre Ugur

title: Bilevel Planning With Learned Symbolic Abstractions From Interaction Data
authors: Fatih Dogangun, Burcu Kilic, Serdar Bahar, Emre Ugur

title: TRaIL-Odom: Tightly Coupled Continuous Time Radar-IMU-LiDAR Odometry With Adaptive Doppler Weighting
authors: Chiyun Noh, Turcan Tuna, William Talbot, Marco Hutter, Laurent Kneip, Ayoung Kim
abstract: Existing radar-LiDAR fusion methods rely on fixed residual weights, even though the informativeness of radar Doppler and LiDAR geometry is scan- and direction-dependent, leading to uniform radar weighting that misallocates Doppler information across translational directions. To address this limitation, we propose two degeneracy-aware Doppler reweighting modules within a tightly coupled Radar-IMU-LiDAR odometry framework: per-point radar reweighting and scan-wise radar gain scheduling. Since geometric degeneracy is directional, we first identify weak translational directions from the LiDAR geometry and reweight individual radar Doppler constraints based on their alignment with the weak subspace. We further adjust the overall radar contribution using LiDAR geometric anisotropy such that radar is emphasized when LiDAR observability is poor and suppressed when LiDAR constraints are already reliable. Across 13 evaluated sequences, TRaIL-Odom achieves state-of-the-art overall performance, with clear advantages in geometrically degenerate scenes. In ablation experiments on three degenerate sequences, combining the two adaptive weighting modules reduces RMSE ATE and RTE by 86.0% and 78.5% relative to the fixed-weight baseline. We make our code and an accompanying dataset publicly available at https://github.com/ChiyunNoh/TRaIL-Odom.

title: Quadruped Obstacle Avoidance and Footstep Planning With Distributed Low-Cost Time-of-Flight Sensors
authors: Giammarco Caroleo, Timothee Mahamoodally, Matteo Manzardo, Jin Jin, Marco Pontin, Matias Mattamala, Renato Vidoni, Perla Maiolino, Maurice Fallon
abstract: Quadruped robots typically rely on depth cameras and LiDAR sensors to map their local environment. However, these sensors have limited close-range coverage, are relatively expensive, and consume significant power. This study investigates whether distributed Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensors can serve as a low-cost alternative to depth cameras for near-field terrain mapping for locomotion and local navigation. We designed a distributed ToF sensing architecture for the ANYbotics ANYmal quadruped, assessed its environment reconstruction accuracy, and benchmarked it against depth cameras for terrain mapping and obstacle avoidance. Distributing these sensors around the robot can also avoid the blind spots of traditional sensors. Our results show that, despite their low resolution and higher measurement noise, distributed ToF sensors can support reliable perceptual locomotion with centimeter-level local mapping accuracy. The proposed sensing strategy provides sufficient geometric information for near-field obstacle avoidance and footstep planning, at substantially lower cost, energy consumption, and system complexity than depth cameras

title: Variable-Structure Soft Actuator for Multi-Mode Grasping
authors: Xuanhao Zhang, Yao Jiantao, Zhang Shuai, Daming Yuan, Chunjie Wei, Chen Xinbo
abstract: Soft actuators are widely used in grasping tasks involving irregularly shaped and fragile objects due to their inherent compliance. However, most existing soft actuators lack shape-morphing capabilities, making it difficult to achieve optimal grasping performance when faced with different operational scenarios. Inspired by the grasping ability of the octopus tentacle, we propose a design and fabrication method for a bending-type soft actuator with switchable deformation capability, termed VSSA (Variable-structure Soft Actuator). The VSSA consists of a structurally variable limiting layer and a folded tube. By altering the structure of the limiting layer, the VSSA can achieve both planar bending motion and spatial helical bending motion. A corresponding theoretical model was established to analyze the deformation modes of the VSSA under different air chamber distance. Furthermore, experiments were conducted to evaluate its motion characteristics, stiffness, tip force, and pull-off force. Based on the VSSA, single-finger, two-finger, and multi-finger grippers were further fabricated, demonstrating effective grasping capabilities for daily objects of various shapes, sizes, and weights. The results indicate that the variable-structure capability endows the grippers with enhanced shape and size adaptability, offering a novel approach to improving the performance of soft grippers.

title: Fetch My Beer: Synthetic-to-Real Hierarchical Policy for Smooth Pick-and-Place
authors: Yingyue Li, Chenyangguang Zhang, Ruida Zhang, Bowen Fu, Guangyao Zhai, Xiangyang Ji
abstract: Many real-world robotic applications require dynamically sensitive manipulation, where success depends not only on reaching a target state but on maintaining stable object dynamics throughout execution. We study the stable transport of liquid-filled containers, where a robot must move objects to target locations while suppressing sloshing and preventing spillage. Unlike conventional pick-and-place, this task imposes stringent requirements on motion smoothness and trajectory-level stability, exposing clear limitations in existing systems. Specifically, fluid simulation remains too costly for online reinforcement learning; human teleoperation introduces unintended accelerations that induce sloshing during imitation learning; and current policy pipelines optimize for task completion rather than dynamic stability. We propose a synthetic-to-real framework coupling physically validated data generation with a hierarchical, diffusion-based controller. The scalable data pipeline synthesizes grasps, filters unstable poses via a vision-language model, and validates transport trajectories through fluid simulation. The policy is organized with a high-level module that translates language and visual observations into SE(3) control targets, and a latent diffusion controller that first plans efficiently in a compact latent space and then decodes dense action chunks, enabling the high control frequency needed for smooth and stable motion. Extensive experiments show our system outperforms state-of-the-art manipulation policies in transport smoothness and dynamic stability. Our project page: https://fetch-my-beer.github.io/

title: LNP: Liquid Network Policy for Humanoid Whole-Body Motion Tracking
authors: Yaoxiang Pu, Yishuai Cai, Yuanheng Zhu, Zhe Hu
abstract: Humanoid whole-body motion tracking is a key capability for agile humanoid control, yet its policy representation remains poorly matched to the temporal structure of the problem. Humanoid motion is inherently continuous-time and multi-timescale, with fast contact transitions, intermediate stabilization dynamics, and longer-horizon motion context, whereas most tracking policies are still optimized as fixed-step discrete-time mappings. We argue that this mismatch is a critical source of brittleness, especially when delayed feedback creates an offset between the current control step and the observed robot state. We propose LNP, a liquid network policy for humanoid whole-body motion tracking. LNP models the actor as a time-aware recurrent policy with a mixed-memory architecture: liquid state updates handle fast action-state dynamics, while an auxiliary memory pathway captures longer-range temporal context. To train this stateful actor stably within Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), we develop a PPO-compatible TBPTT procedure that restores recurrent states, uses overlapping windows and burn-in, and evaluates losses only on valid sequence steps. Experiments on four humanoid tracking tasks show that LNP achieves a 100% success rate across all tasks and obtains the lowest global tracking error on each task. Under injected observation delays from 0 to 160 ms, LNP exhibits slower tracking-error growth and more gradual reward degradation than feedforward, recurrent, and motion-prior baselines. These results demonstrate that the proposed mixed-memory recurrent representation improves tracking accuracy and robustness to stale feedback without explicit delay compensation.

title: SP-VoxelDet: Channel-Efficient Fully Sparse 3D Object Detection Via Partial Convolution
authors: Xing Chen, Xinsheng He
abstract: Efficient and reliable 3D perception is fundamental for autonomous robotic systems under strict onboard computational constraints. Although sparse convolution exploits spatial sparsity in LiDAR point clouds, existing methods largely overlook channel redundancy, creating unnecessary overhead on resource-limited platforms. We present SP-VoxelDet, a channel-aware lightweight framework for fully sparse 3D object detection. The core idea is to reduce channel-wise redundancy in sparse voxel representations. Its core operator, PC-SubMConv3d, applies submanifold sparse convolution to only a subset of feature channels while directly propagating the remainder, reducing computation without altering the spatial receptive field. We further introduce a stage-wise channel allocation strategy that applies stronger reduction in early geometric layers and restores full-channel computation in deeper semantic layers. A lightweight late-stage sparse multi-scale fusion module uses normalized learnable scale weights to improve cross-scale aggregation with limited overhead. On KITTI, SP-VoxelDet reduces parameters by 31.1% and improves inference speed by 13.2% over a strong fully sparse baseline, with only a 0.13 mAP decrease. On nuScenes validation, SP-VoxelDet achieves 59.53 mAP and 66.38 NDS, with only 0.47 mAP and 0.72 NDS decreases relative to the baseline, showing that the channel-efficient design remains competitive on a larger-scale benchmark. Improved pedestrian detection suggests particular benefits for small and sparse targets. In an embedded study using a Velodyne VLP-16 LiDAR and NVIDIA Jetson Orin within a ROS 2 pipeline, SP-VoxelDet achieves higher end-to-end throughput under identical conditions. These results indicate that channel-aware sparse computation is effective for resource-constrained LiDAR perception.

title: TransDex: Interaction Geometry Enables Robust Visuo-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation of Transparent Objects
authors: Fengguan Li, Yifan Ma, Chen Qian, Wentao Rao, Weiwei Shang
abstract: This paper presents TransDex, an interaction-geometry-aware 3D visuo-tactile fusion motor policy for dexterous manipulation of transparent objects. Dexterous manipulation enables complex tasks but is fundamentally challenged by hand–object interaction geometric ambiguity caused by self-occlusion, severe depth noise, and depth information loss when manipulating transparent objects. To overcome these challenges, we first propose a self-supervised point cloud reconstruction pre-training approach based on Transformer, which accurately recovers the 3D structure of objects from interaction point clouds of dexterous hands, even when random noise and large-scale masking are added. Building on this, TransDex is constructed in which perceptual encoding adopts a fine-grained hierarchical scheme and multi-round attention mechanisms adaptively fuse features of the robotic arm and dexterous hand to enable differentiated motion prediction. Experimental results conducted on a real robotic system demonstrate that TransDex outperforms existing baseline methods, which successfully validate the generalization capabilities of the proposed method.

title: Vision-Based Tactile Sensing for the Perception of the Object's Compliance and Hardness
authors: Muxing Huang, Zibin Chen, Weiliang Xu, Zilan Li, Yuanzhi Zhou, Guoyuan Zhou, Wenjing Chen, Xinming Li
abstract: Object compliance perception enables the identification of soft materials, supporting tasks such as fruit detection and assisted medical palpation. Compliance perception requires sensing an object's deformation and contact forces. Existing vision-based tactile sensing for compliance perception usually depends only on force or deformation. However, deformation-based approaches cannot reliably quantify object compliance, while force-based methods are overly sensitive to geometric variations. To address these limitations, this paper presents a framework that fuses temporal force sequences and deformation field information. Specifically, time-varying contact forces are inferred from tactile image sequences via a neural network, while deformation characteristics are encoded using depth maps. Crucially, the temporal force sequence is used as a dynamic force-response feature for compliance recognition. In standard experiments, the force prediction error reaches 0.06 N within a measurement range of 12 N. The proposed method achieves a 98.0% Shore-hardness classification accuracy for samples ranging from 10 HA to 80 HA. In practical scenarios, including abnormal fruit detection and soft matter, the overall accuracy exceeds 98.5%. This method improves the compliance perception ability of artificial tactile systems and facilitates their deployment in embodied perception applications.

title: FluidTac: A Vision-Based Arrayed Artificial Lateral Line Sensor for Underwater Ego-Motion Estimation
authors: Zhipeng Fei, Yicheng Lin, Hengpeng Xie, Cong Li, Bin Han
abstract: Underwater ego-motion estimation is crucial for achieving autonomous navigation in Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs). Obtaining continuous and robust velocity observations in shallow, acoustically and visually constrained environments remains an open problem, especially for compact platforms where acoustic bottom-tracking and vision-based methods are prone to degradation. To this end, this letter proposes a vision-based arrayed Artificial Lateral Line (ALL) sensor named FluidTac, capable of obtaining reliable odometry in acoustically constrained shallow waters. In terms of sensing mechanism, the system utilizes a circularly distributed array of passive propellers to translate local flow into rotation. A built-in camera tracks their angular velocities to estimate the AUV's motion. We employ a neural network that regresses the body's forward velocity, which is then fused with inertial data to achieve robust ego-motion estimation. Underwater experiments demonstrate FluidTac's accuracy in perceiving flow velocity and direction. To validate the system's performance, we integrated FluidTac into an AUV for real-world lake experiments. The results indicate that the system maintains reliable state estimation in shallow, turbid, and unstructured environments, without relying on acoustic bottom-tracking or visual features. This provides a low-cost and high-efficiency solution for AUV ego-motion estimation.

title: Learning Spatially Ambiguous Trajectories From Demonstrations Via Phase-Modulated Dynamical Systems

title: Electromechanical Co-Design Toward Realizing Autonomous Insect-Scale Flapping-Wing Micro-Aerial Vehicles
authors: Jalil Morris, Christian Chan, Georgios Kyriazidis, Arjun Batra, Aryan Naveen, Robert Wood, Gage Hills
abstract: Autonomous insect-scale ($) flapping-wing micro-aerial vehicles (FWMAVs) represent an emerging robotic platform with potential applications in areas such as environmental protection and search and rescue. However, achieving full autonomy — requiring simultaneous integration of sensors, controllers, actuation, power conversion, and an energy source — in insect-scale FWMAVs is challenging due to the stringent size, weight, and power (SWaP) constraints that must be satisfied to sustain flight. Furthermore, manufacturing the components required for autonomous operations at the insect-scale is time-intensive, emphasizing the importance of electromechanical co-design before fabrication, to identify the most promising systems and avoid wasting time on non-flightworthy designs. To address these challenges, we: (1) present a holistic electromechanical co-design framework to explore a large, 12-dimensional design space of electrical and mechanical parameters for identifying autonomous insect-scale FWMAV designs; (2) identify two sets of electrical and mechanical design parameters corresponding to systems that are highly promising to realize autonomous insect-scale FWMAVs – (i) a 1 $\mathrm{g}$ design with 570 $\mathrm{s}$ flight time, and (ii) a 623 $\text{mg}$ design with a 91 $\mathrm{s}$ flight time; and (3) identify Flight Time to Mass Ratio (FTMR) as an effective figure of merit (FoM) for designers to optimize, in order to identify flightworthy autonomous FWMAV designs. We construct a parameterized model for FTMR and show, among the top designs with highest FTMR, our parameterized model predicts FTMR within $\mathrm{7\%}$ of the values reported by our detailed framework. Thus, we demonstrate that maximizing FTMR through our parameterized model enables designers to efficiently navigate the large design space and rapidly converge on flightworthy designs.

title: Step Into the Unknown: Online Visual-Physical Bayesian Inference for Open-World Terrain Perception
authors: Zeyu Zhang, Kehui Ma, Zhen Sun, Chaoran Xiong, Fangyu Jiang, Yunjie Lai, Junjie Wang, Ling Pei
abstract: Reliable terrain perception is fundamental for the embodied navigation of legged robots in open-world environments. However, dynamically discovering unbounded terrain categories from streaming visual and proprioceptive data remains challenging. Existing methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting, rely on computationally expensive experience replay, or use heuristic rules to resolve cross-modal conflicts. To address these limitations, we propose an online multimodal Bayesian inference framework for open-world latent terrain perception. We employ a Dirichlet Process (DP) prior that adaptively expands the terrain space for unknown categories. To retain historical knowledge without experience replay overhead, we formulate a Dynamic Belief State based on conjugate priors, which compresses visual-physical observations into fixed-size sufficient statistics to enable efficient recursive updates. Furthermore, we derive an analytical posterior log-odds hypothesis test to evaluate whether an observation is known or novel by weighting multimodal evidence. Experiments on a quadruped robot in both simulation and real-world environments demonstrate its effectiveness, yielding a severe error rate of 0.013, an average retention rate of 97.1%, and a Bayesian backend inference time of approximately 1 ms.

title: STRAP: A Task-Level Autonomous Suture-Thread Pulling System for Robot-Assisted Minimally Invasive Suturing
authors: Mei Feng, Haoju Li, Chao Han, Hao Liu, Xiuquan Lu, Yao Li, Yitong Zhang, Zhiwu Han, Dong He
abstract: Suture-thread pulling is necessary yet underexplored in robot-assisted minimally invasive suturing. After needle insertion and extraction, the thread must be pulled to approximate the wound edges while preserving sufficient length for knot tying or continuous suturing. This paper presents Suture Thread Robotic Autonomous Pulling (STRAP), a task-level autonomous framework executed by an assisted patient-side manipulator (assisted PSM). STRAP generates grasping and pulling strategies from stereo-endoscopic three-dimensional reconstruction and a simplified geometric representation of the target thread. Pulling termination jointly considers grasp verification, realized pulling length, insertion-side residual thread length, visual wound-state classification, and local geometric consistency. Ex vivo porcine-liver experiments yielded a 95.0% first-attempt grasping success rate, and all 60 pulling attempts were completed after retrying when necessary. The mean total pulling time was close to expert operation and shorter than novice operation. In blinded wound-closure assessment, the Fine rates were 93.3% for STRAP, 90.0% for the expert, and 70.0% for the novice. Under the present ex vivo conditions, constrained task-level autonomy provided repeatable assisted suture-thread pulling while maintaining acceptable visual wound-closure quality.

title: Tissue-Aware Sensorless 6D Force/Torque Estimation Via Cross-Modal Fusion for Robot-Assisted NOTES Biopsy
authors: Yingxuan Zhang, Qi Jiang, Jie Wang, Rammah Ibrahim
abstract: Stable sensorless force estimation is critical for natural orifice transluminal endoscopic surgery (NOTES) biopsy, where biopsy needles interact with soft tissue through constrained endoscopic channels. However, the relationship among tissue deformation, robot motion, and interaction force varies across tissue states, so similar observations may correspond to different interaction forces. To address this issue, we propose TCF-Net, a tissue-aware cross-modal framework for online 6D force/torque estimation from endoscopic RGB images and robot state. Tissue-state supervision guides the shared representation toward tissue-dependent force–deformation–motion relationships, while gated cross-modal fusion adaptively integrates visual and robot-state cues. A synchronized multimodal dataset of 1385 sequences is constructed for constrained-channel robot-assisted needle insertion, covering multiple needle gauges, insertion angles, insertion speeds, and tissue states. The framework is evaluated through estimation, generalization, robustness, and qualitative cross-platform deployment experiments. TCF-Net achieves a mean force RMSE of 0.0157 N, a mean torque RMSE of 0.0004 Nm, and an average inference latency of 10 ms. Compared with the model without tissue-state assistance, TCF-Net reduces the mean force RMSE by 34.3% and improves the $F_{z}$ Pearson correlation by 15.7%, demonstrating the potential of tissue-aware cross-modal learning for sensorless force estimation in constrained surgical environments.

title: A Liouville Equation-Based Hybrid Method for Uncertainty-Aware Vehicle Motion Prediction
authors: Mingze Miao, Shulin Zhang, Zhishuai Yin, Yuanhao Kuang, Linzhen Nie, Chengbo Yao
abstract: Robust prediction of the uncertain motion states of surrounding vehicles remains a fundamental challenge in autonomous driving. To address this challenge, we introduce the Liouville Equation (LE) into motion prediction to characterize the evolution of uncertain states governed by probability conservation, and propose a hybrid mechanism-learning paradigm. Specifically, we establish the LE as the mechanistic framework to ensure the physical consistency of state evolution. To provide the required dynamic driving force within this framework, we design a Transformer-based architecture to learn an adaptive context-conditioned state vector field (SVF), thereby overcoming the limitations of purely mechanistic methods in capturing system dynamics under complex driving scenarios. During the LE-based evolution of uncertain motion states, the learned SVF governs their geometric transport in the state space, while the divergence of the SVF dynamically adjusts the probabilistic weight associated with each motion state. Experimental results on both simulation and real-world data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves robust prediction performance, effectively captures potential collision risks, and thereby improves the safety of downstream planned trajectories.

title: SparKLoc: Sparse Key-Gaussian Matching for 3D Gaussian-Based Visual Localization

title: 3D-RobOstrich: An Ostrich-Inspired 3D Flexible Manipulator With a Lateral Stabilization Mechanism
authors: Tomoya Uchiike, Kazashi Nakano, Max Austin, Yasuo Kuniyoshi, Kohei Nakajima
abstract: Flexible manipulators based on bio-inspired approaches are useful for tasks in uncertain environments and those involving contact. Tendon-driven mechanisms are widely used as a simple method to actuate flexible manipulators; however, when these manipulators operate in 3D space, unexpected lateral buckling caused by gravity and tendon tension becomes a significant problem. In this study, inspired by the function of the ostrich neck, which dexterously manipulates a flexible neck against gravity, we proposed a lateral stabilization mechanism that improves lateral stability while reducing its resistance to flexible dorsoventral bending movements. Furthermore, we developed “3D-RobOstrich”, an ostrich-inspired 3D flexible manipulator equipped with this mechanism at each joint; modeling and experiments confirmed that the mechanism expands the upward workspace and prevents sudden lateral bending. Additionally, using this manipulator, we demonstrated 3D reaching in environments with obstacles and mobile manipulation integrated with a quadruped robot, confirming that flexible reaching motions can be achieved while ensuring lateral stability.

title: MonoTemp3D: Lightweight Short-Horizon Temporal Enhancement for Streaming Monocular 3D Car Detection
authors: Jiaying Li, Tong Liu, Xiaodong Guo, Yike Li
abstract: Monocular 3D object detection (M3OD) is attractive for autonomous driving and resource-constrained robotic platforms due to its low hardware cost. While temporal cues can alleviate depth ambiguity, dense feature matching and explicit motion estimation introduce substantial latency and limit low-latency deployment. To alleviate this burden, we introduce MonoTemp3D, a lightweight dual-level temporal enhancement framework tailored to causal streaming query-based monocular 3D car detection. It efficiently exploits short-term temporal continuity and compact historical representations while preserving low-latency inference. To aggregate informative historical features without heavy pixel-wise matching, an asymmetric cross-scale temporal fusion module is proposed to employ sparse deformable attention as an implicit, task-driven temporal sampler. In addition, we introduce a context-aware query updating mechanism to propagate high-confidence historical object queries as instance-level priors and update them using current observations to stabilize 3D detection. Experiments on KITTI Tracking, KITTI 3D and nuScenes show that MonoTemp3D outperforms representative image-based and video-based M3OD methods. MonoTemp3D achieves inference latencies of 34 ms on an RTX 3090 GPU and 43.5 ms on a Jetson Orin NX (TensorRT, FP16).

title: SpatioDenoiser: Position-Guided Denoising via Spatial Audio Memory for Anomalous Sound Detection in Mobile Robots
authors: Koki Shoda, Jun Younes Louhi Kasahara, Takuya Igaue, Tomohito Hoshii, Masayoshi Kinoshita, Risa Koda, Shota Shimizu, Shinji Kanda, Hajime Asama, Qi An, Atsushi Yamashita
abstract: We introduce SpatioDenoiser, a position-guided denoising framework for Anomalous Sound Detection (ASD) for robotic inspections. While detecting machine anomalies using sound is a key objective for robotic inspections, its performance is degraded by the pervasive background noise in industrial facilities, making the suppression of such noise necessary. Language-queried source separation is a promising approach to this problem, yet it requires human operators to manually tune text prompts for each machine, hindering automation. To address this, we introduce SpatioDenoiser, a position-guided denoising framework that eliminates the need for manual tuning. SpatioDenoiser constructs a spatial audio memory that maps the robot’s coordinates to the acoustic features of normal sounds expected at each location. This memory automatically generates an acoustic query from the robot’s current position, which guides a pre-trained extraction module to selectively suppress background noise while retaining anomaly-relevant acoustic features for downstream ASD. Experiments on a public dataset and in a pilot plant yielded higher observed values for the evaluated denoising and AutoEncoder-based ASD metrics than the conventional methods.

title: Path Passing Sequence Search for Lifelong Multi-Agent Pathfinding with Uncertain Delays
authors: Zhehong Zhang, Guangyu Piao, Songhao Piao
abstract: The Lifelong Multi-Agent Path Finding (LMAPF) problem in practice faces significant challenges due to uncertain delays and the interleaving of planning and execution. Traditional solvers often rely on precise time-step reservations, which are prone to failure when agents deviate from their schedules, leading to inaccurate collision predictions between planning and executing agents. To address this limitation, this letter proposes a Path-Passing-Sequence Search (PPSS) framework that constructs robust passing sequences directly during the planning phase without strict reliance on time steps. PPSS extends the A* algorithm by expanding the search state space to determine spatial routes and valid insertion positions within existing passing orders simultaneously. Furthermore, a novel collision prediction strategy is introduced to evaluate potential conflicts and deadlock cycles by analyzing the relative passing ranks of Anchor-Anchor Movement Units (AAMUs). Extensive experiments in discrete-time settings and a preliminary real-world deployment in a continuous-time setting demonstrate that PPSS effectively generates collision-free paths and maintains safe passing orders even under practical uncertain delays.

title: Contact-Guided Exploration for Non-Prehensile Locomanipulation With Multi-Critic RL
authors: Simone Tolomei, Mayank Mittal, Franco Angelini, Manolo Garabini, Paolo Salaris, Marco Hutter
abstract: Non-prehensile manipulation offers versatile skills for moving and rearranging heavy or bulky objects, particularly when combined with a mobile manipulation platform. However, both model-based and model-free approaches struggle with the complex hybrid dynamics and the sparsity of the contact in these tasks. To address these challenges, we propose a contact-guided exploration strategy implemented within a Multi-Critic Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework. A dedicated exploration critic is trained with a dense contact-seeking reward that guides the end-effector toward meaningful contact points; its influence is progressively decayed to recover a task-optimal policy. We obtain candidate interaction points from a general-purpose grasping algorithm, enabling the exploration mechanism to generalise across various object geometries. We evaluate the approach on multiple tasks, including box pushing, chair transportation, and a dishwasher opening task. Finally, we validate the chair transportation policy through extensive experiments on a quadrupedal mobile manipulator, demonstrating deployable non-prehensile manipulation in the real world.

title: Fault-Tolerant, Rigidity-Preserving Control of Inflatable Truss Robots
authors: James Wade, Isaac Weaver, Mihai Stanciu, Nathan Usevitch
abstract: Isoperimetric robotic trusses can adapt to different tasks and environments due to their high strength-to-weight ratio and the ability to reconfigure dramatically into new shapes. However, motor failures in operational environments can severely limit capability if not properly addressed. This letter presents a fault-tolerant control framework for an inflatable robotic truss that maintains functionality despite motor failures, demonstrated through three key contributions. First, we extend the kinematic optimization to handle arbitrary combinations of motor failures by imposing equality constraints to ensure failed actuators are not used. Second, we introduce discrete-time control barrier function (DTCBF) constraints that, under the assumed kinematic model, mathematically guarantee structural rigidity while maximizing workspace utilization. Third, we implement closed-loop position control using onboard encoder feedback and a forward-kinematics-based state estimator, improving positional accuracy in the presence of disturbances. We validate our approach through simulation and hardware experiments on a 2D isoperimetric truss testbed. For a 2D configuration with 6 actuators, we demonstrate >62% workspace preservation under single-motor failures, a >22% reduction in tracking RMSE using failure-aware closed-loop control relative to the fully functional open-loop baseline, and a 39% closed-loop RMSE reduction over failure-unaware open-loop control under unmodeled partial actuator degradation. These results establish a foundation for more robust and resilient isoperimetric truss robots operating under degraded actuation.

title: Decoupled Time-Delay Koopman Learning for Adaptive Model Predictive Control of Soft Manipulators
authors: Yuxuan Chen, Yunpeng Zhu, Jianda Han, Yu Dang
abstract: The modeling and control of soft pneumatic manipulators present significant challenges due to their inherent compliance and history-dependent hysteresis. While the Koopman operator theory offers a promising solution by embedding these nonlinear dynamics into a linear framework, conventional Koopman approaches are limited by static models that fail to adapt to time-varying environments. To address this limitation, this study proposes a decoupled time-delay Koopman learning framework integrated with adaptive model predictive control. Specifically, a neural network with time-delay embedding is constructed to explicitly capture memory effects inherent in soft materials. Crucially, by incorporating a variance-covariance regularization strategy, the method enforces feature orthogonality during the learning of time-delay dynamics. This decoupling significantly reduces linear redundancy, thereby improving the numerical conditioning of the recursive least-squares updates and enhancing the efficiency of the feature dimension. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves improved trajectory tracking accuracy and robustness, especially in low-dimensional lifting spaces. A Diamond robot simulation in SOFA and a physical tube manipulation task were conducted to validate the effectiveness of the proposed controller.

title: ARCGym: Benchmarking Deep Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Robotic Colonoscopy
authors: Guanglin Ji, Martina Finocchiaro, Kenny Erleben, Hang Yin
abstract: Simulations for learning-based autonomous colonoscopic navigation focus mainly on fully actuated capsule robots, failing to capture the contact-rich navigation of long and flexible clinical colonoscopes. We present the Autonomous Robotic Colonoscopy Gym (ARCGym), an open-source reinforcement learning environment and benchmark for image-based navigation in clinically derived deformable colon anatomies. ARCGym supports multiple types of colonoscope robots, spanning capsule robots and flexible endoscopes, with this work focusing on flexible endoscopes including magnetic-driven tip actuation and clinically used proximally translational actuation. This work includes five CT-reconstructed colons representing typical clinical scenarios, a set of clinically meaningful navigation subtasks, and unified success metrics. We introduce a reward combining depth-based lumen alignment with a lumen-visibility score to improve learning under occlusions. Experiments across tasks, robots, and anatomies show that autonomous navigation remains challenging for both magnetic-driven and proximal-insertion flexible robots, with proximal-insertion actuation remaining an open problem.

title: Real-Time Flapping-Wing Motion State Estimation and Modulation Control Using Inertial Sensors
authors: Jinchuan Du, Peng Tang, Jianghao Wu
abstract: Real-time acquisition of the flapping phase and frequency is crucial for advanced wing kinematics control in Flapping-Wing Micro Air Vehicles (FWMAVs). Constrained by the absence of sensors for direct stroke angle measurement, indirect-drive FWMAVs are limited to open-loop averaged wing kinematics control. They require additional servo mechanisms for attitude stabilization and face challenges in precise flapping frequency regulation. Inspired by biological perception, we propose a vibration-based flapping state estimation method. Relying solely on acceleration data from an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), this approach achieves low-latency, real-time estimation of the flapping phase and frequency via Phase-Locked Loop (PLL) and Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithms. Building upon this, we further introduce a flapping modulation method for pitch control, thereby eliminating the need for additional pitch actuators. Furthermore, we implement a closed-loop flapping frequency controller with feedforward compensation. Flight experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves highly accurate estimation under variable-frequency flapping conditions, with the EKF estimation achieving a dynamic frequency tracking error below 1%, resulting in hovering pitch attitude oscillations within $\pm 3^{\circ }$. This approach provides a promising solution for the structural simplification and performance enhancement of highly integrated FWMAVs.

title: Anti-Gravity Walking by a Flying Humanoid Robot Via Thrust-Rate Input Whole-Body Model Predictive Control
authors: Kazuki Sugihara, Kei Okada
abstract: Flying humanoids are expected to perform tasks in diverse environments, while their existing locomotion is mainly limited to aerial flight and ground walking. The capability to move in complex three-dimensional space can greatly expand their application range. For such walking motion on ceilings and similar anti-gravity environments, whole-body MPC is effective. However, the discontinuous changes in dynamic structure accompanying contact switching during walking can induce thrust spikes, resulting in control instability. Therefore, in this work, we propose and implement a real-time whole-body MPC framework for anti-gravity bipedal walking. First, we formulate whole-body MPC using the time derivative of thrust, namely thrust-rate, as the control input. This formulation guarantees continuity of the thrust trajectory during contact switching while preserving the sparse structure of the optimal control problem for fast computation. Second, we address the lack of natural support forces in anti-gravity environments. We introduce lower bounds on the foot-normal component of the contact force, and smoothly transfer them during the doublesupport phase. Finally, we implement the proposed framework and demonstrate anti-gravity walking by a flying humanoid through simulation and a hardware experiment. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of multi-contact whole-body MPC for a transformable aerial robot and walking by a flying humanoid beyond the ground.
